llm.summary: This skill is a real Android automation bridge, but it grants broad persistent control of a connected phone with weak local isolation and under-disclosed risky defaults.

dimensions.detail: Reading screens, tapping, scrolling, typing, screenshots, OCR, and Appium/uiautomator2 control are mostly coherent with the stated purpose of controlling Android apps, but they are high-impact capabilities for any connected device and app.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The main documentation discloses broad Android control and screenshots, but it does not clearly document all exposed daemon actions such as js_scroll, ocr_tap, and find_book_button or the security implications of typed input, OCR, and screenshots on sensitive apps.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The start script is straightforward and user-invoked, but it kills existing bridge processes, removes shared /tmp state files, starts Appium, and launches a background daemon.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill starts Appium with --allow-insecure all and --relaxed-security and exposes automation over localhost, which is broader than necessary for a generic local bridge and expands the local attack surface.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The daemon persists in the background and uses predictable /tmp command, response, lock, log, and screenshot paths without authentication or ownership/permission checks, allowing local process interference and potential exposure of screen contents.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you intentionally want a persistent local agent that can read and control a connected Android device. Avoid using it on banking, messaging, password, payment, or account-recovery screens, and review the /tmp IPC/screenshot handling and Appium insecure flags before running it on a shared or multi-user machine.
llm.findings:
[AST4] expected: Use of subprocess for adb/Appium is expected for Android automation, but the hard-coded insecure Appium flags and fixed /tmp screenshot paths are not well contained for a persistent device-control bridge.
[TT2] unexpected: The file-based /tmp command and response channel is a real local control-channel concern because any same-host process may be able to inject commands or read responses if permissions allow.
[SDI-1] unexpected: The artifact supports additional capabilities beyond the prominent command list, including OCR tapping and JavaScript scrolling, so the user-facing scope is incomplete.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Starting Appium with globally insecure and relaxed-security options is broader than the stated bridge purpose requires and is not clearly surfaced as an opt-in risk.
[SQP-2] expected: Screenshots, OCR, typing, and background automation fit the tool's purpose, but the artifacts do not provide enough warning, consent guidance, secure storage, or local IPC controls for those sensitive operations.
